title: The maximal fibre degree locus is open with finite restriction
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Suppose $m\in\mathbb N$ bounds its finite fibre degrees [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. Then $U=\{s\in S:\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O)=m\}$ is open, and the restriction $X\times_S U\to U$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: For each point of degree m choose an etale neighbourhood on which the pullback is finite locally free of degree m. Fibre-degree invariance puts the entire image in the degree-m locus. These images are open, contain their chosen points, and cover the locus; their union proves openness.

Factor the neighbourhood maps through the open locus by the open-immersion lift. Cancellation shows these factors are etale, and the factors jointly cover the open locus. Paste the restriction pullback with each covering pullback to obtain the original neighbourhood pullback. Its canonical pullback isomorphism transports finiteness and the constant fibre degree. Apply etale descent of finite local freeness of degree m and retain its finiteness component.
